IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON CLOUD COMPUTING 1 Empirical Systems Characterization of Post-Quantum Session Pooling, Single-Ciphertext CKKS Retrieval, and Transport Fallback Across Cloud-Edge Vector-SQL Streams Preecha Noiumkar, Member, IEEE Abstract—Securing cloud-edge relational and vector retrieval with post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and approximate homomorphic encryption creates coupled trade-offs across handshake latency, wire size, recall, and middlebox resilience. We present CAPQ-Pareto, an empirical systems study characterizing hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768 and ML-DSA-65 session pooling, asymmetric INT8 query quantization, single-ciphertext (1-CT) slot-aggregated RNS-CKKS search, and transport selection across PostgreSQL 18.6 HNSW and OpenFHE. Across a 256-run factorial design, 500-query CKKS controls, RAPL metrology, and three-region wide-area evaluations, four findings emerge. First, persistent PQC session pooling dominates service-level compliance (+52.15 percentage points, Monte Carlo block-randomization p=0.0005), while single-MTU INT8 quantization tightens 95th-percentile error bounds by 5.39x–22.76x over Holder bounds. Second, 1-CT slot aggregation at N=8192 cuts response traffic 7.05x (909.33 to 129.01 KiB) and client decryption 5.56x, reducing net latency below a 423–464 Mbps downlink crossover. Third, plaintext-versus-CKKS controls confirm negligible homomorphic noise loss (at most 0.0052), showing that recall decay from 0.788 (5k) to 0.550 (100k vectors, 224 slots) stems from fixed candidate budgets. Fourth, static pooled UDP+INT8+1-CT matches or outperforms bandit exploration on normal links, whereas RFC 9308 timeout-to-TCP fallback and contextual bandits recover compliance under enterprise UDP policing. Index Terms—Post-quantum TLS, approximate homomorphic encryption, vector databases, QUIC/UDP fallback, contextual bandits, empirical systems measurement. ✦ 1 I NTRODUCTION C LOUD - HOSTED retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and operational analytics increasingly serve mixed request streams combining structured SQL lookups, JSON document reads, public approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) vector search, and privacy-sensitive embedding queries [1], [2], [3]. Hardening such pipelines against harvest-now-decrypt-later adversaries requires migrating transport handshakes to NIST FIPS 203 Module-Lattice Key- Encapsulation (ML-KEM) [4] and FIPS 204 Digital Signatures (ML-DSA) [5], while protecting confidential query coordinates from untrusted cloud operators motivates approximate Ring- LWE homomorphic encryption via Cheon–Kim–Kim–Song (CKKS) [6], [7]. When deployed together over wide-area networks (WANs), these mechanisms interact non-trivially. Fresh hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768 handshakes authenticated by ML-DSA-65 certificate chains exceed standard 10-segment TCP initial congestion windows [8], [9]. In the confidential search tier, returning unaggregated SIMD inner-product ciphertexts inflates response payloads to nearly 1 MiB per query, whereas compacting scores into a single ciphertext • P. Meanwhile, user-space UDP/QUIC framing [10], [11], [12] eliminates TCP head-of-line (HOL) stalls under ran- dom wireless packet loss, yet enterprise firewalls frequently rate-police or block UDP bursts on port 443, requiring TCP fallback as specified in IETF RFC 9308 [13]. A common pitfall in systems-for-ML papers is over- attributing performance gains to adaptive learning con- trollers when static architectural engineering accounts for most of the improvement, or masking recall limitations behind composite stream averages. In this work, we take a deliberately candid, measurement-driven approach. We evaluate where static mechanisms suffice, under what exact network conditions protocol switching is necessary, and where fundamental candidate-budget limits arise in en- crypted ANN search. Summary of Empirical Contributions: 1) Quantified PQC Session Amortization and Single-MTU INT8 Bounds: We benchmark hybrid OpenSSL 3 . 5 . 5 + liboqs session pooling, ML-DSA-44/65/87 authentication framing, and cross-ISA native C AES-256-GCM vs. ChaCha20-Poly1305 goodput on x86 64 and Cloud ARM64. We prove exact conditional ( ≤ ∆ 2 q /4 ) and marginal ( ∆ 2 q /6 ) inner-product error variances for asymmetric INT8 query quantization (Proposition 1), demonstrating 5.39× (SIFT1M, 128 d) and 22.76× (BGE-M3, 1024 d) tighter 95th-percentile bounds than IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON CLOUD COMPUTING worst-case Hölder inequalities alongside million- vector PostgreSQL 18.6 HNSW benchmarks. 2) True 1-CT Slot-Aggregated RNS-CKKS Retrieval, Plaintext Noise Decomposition, and Bandwidth Crossover: Using native C++ OpenFHE at ring di- mension N = 8192 ( log 2 Q = 140 ≤ 218 bits, 128-bit classic security), server-side SIMD block masking, rotation, and slot summation compress responses from 909.33 KiB to 129.01 KiB ( 7.05× ) and cut client decryption from 3.28 ms to 0.59 ms, trading +15.0 ms of server compute. We derive the analytical downlink crossover goodput ( B ⋆ = 423 – 464 Mbps) and decouple index candidate-budget loss from CKKS approximation noise ( |∆R CKKS | ≤ 0.0052 ) across 5 k, 25 k, and 100 k corpora, including negative scaling results under fixed slot budgets. 3) Per-Class SLA Accounting, RFC 9308 Rule Fallback, and Multi-Region WAN Provenance: We formalize per-class SLA indicators (eliminating cross-class accuracy averaging), unify cloud CPU+egress cost modeling across live cellular/wireless (Track 1, 1,440 queries) and calibrated namespace (Track 2, 2,304 queries) campaigns, audit empirical leakage attacks (A1--A3) and IND-CPA D boundaries [14], and benchmark 5D contextual bandits [15], [16], [17] directly against a stateless RFC 9308 timeout- triggered TCP fallback rule. 2 R ELATED W ORK Table 1 contrasts CAPQ-Pareto against four intersecting research threads. Post-Quantum TLS and QUIC Measurements. Paquin et al. [8], Sikeridis et al. [9], and Sosnowski et al. [18] demon- strated over emulated and live Internet paths that while hybrid lattice key exchange (ML-KEM-768) fits within a single MTU, post-quantum X.509 certificate chains (ML-DSA) span 9 – 11 Ethernet frames and incur multi-RTT penalties above 1% – 3% packet loss. Complementary IETF standards such as RFC 8879 certificate compression [21] shrink X.509 metadata and extension overhead by roughly 15% – 22% , although lattice public keys and signatures have high entropy and compress minimally [9]. Our study extends transport- only benchmarks into persistent database session pooling and end-to-end query SLA attribution. Encrypted Nearest-Neighbor Search. Fully oblivious FHE/MPC vector search such as SANNS [19] hides cluster access patterns via cryptographic shuffling at multi-hundred- millisecond compute and high communication cost. Con- versely, Tiptoe [20] scales private web search by letting clients route queries to coarse K-means clusters and evalu- ating linear inner products via homomorphic encryption / PIR, trading cluster-ID exposure for practical latency. CAPQ-Pareto investigates this cluster-routed, coordinate- confidential regime using Ring-LWE RNS-CKKS [6], [7] and SPANN-style padded buckets [22], explicitly quantifying equal-candidate-budget controls against disjoint K-means, corpus-scaling recall limits up to 100,000 vectors, and Zipfian frequency-inference attacks. 2 QUIC Applicability and Middlebox Fallback. Langley et al. [10] and IETF RFC 9000/9002 [11], [12] showed that UDP- based stream framing avoids TCP HOL blocking during loss bursts. However, RFC 9308 [13] emphasizes that enterprise middleboxes frequently drop or rate-limit sustained UDP flows, mandating resilient fallback to TCP. We directly implement and test a stateless RFC 9308 timeout-triggered TCP fallback baseline alongside online bandits. Contextual Bandits in Non-Stationary Systems. Stationary LinUCB [15], Sliding-Window UCB [16], and exponentially discounted D-LinUCB [17] balance exploration and exploita- tion under varying reward dynamics. Our empirical evalua- tion reveals an instructive nuanced result: when lagged RTT and loss features already expose network state in the context vector, stationary LinUCB and deterministic RFC 9308 rules match or outperform discounted bandits without suffering high-RTT TCP exploration tails. 3 S YSTEM M ODEL , S ECURITY S COPE , T RANS - PORT S TACK , AND P ER -C LASS SLA 3.1 Workload Model and Coordinate-Confidential Secu- rity Scope Figure 1 depicts the architecture. Arriving edge queries q t belong to syntactic classes c t ∈ { sql , json , vec , conf } . Relational point lookups (sql), document fetches (json), and public semantic vector searches (vec) execute over PQC- authenticated encrypted channels against a trusted cloud database (PostgreSQL 18.6 with pgvector 0.8.1), protecting data in transit. For confidential vector queries ( c t = conf), the cloud server is modeled as honest-but-curious. Query embeddings q ∈ S D−1 are encrypted client-side under RLWE RNS-CKKS satisfying the 128-bit classic security standard (HEStd 128 classic [7]). To avoid exhaustive O(N vec ) homomorphic scans, the client holds coarse cluster centroids ( 48 KiB at K c = 96 , 640 KiB at K c = 1,280 ) and requests r padded buckets B r (q) = (b 1 , . . . , b r ) , each padded with dummy zero vectors to uniform cardinality B max ( M = rB max evaluated slots). IND-CPA D Considerations for Approximate HE. Li and Micciancio [14] proved that approximate homomorphic schemes such as CKKS can fail passive key-recovery security under decryption-result exposure (IND-CPA D ) if an adver- sary observes exact decrypted floating-point outputs and ex- ploits linear noise equations. In CAPQ-Pareto’s single-tenant edge-client architecture, the CKKS secret key resides strictly on the client, and decrypted candidate similarity scores are consumed locally for top- k selection without ever returning raw decrypted scalars or decryption-oracle responses to the cloud server. Consequently, the cloud server’s view reduces strictly to standard IND-CPA ciphertexts plus coarse bucket indices B r (q) . Extending this architecture to multi- tenant scenarios where decrypted scores are shared across mutually distrusting parties would require explicit noise flooding (supported via NOISE FLOODING MULTIPARTY in OpenFHE [7]) before output release. For 0-RTT session resumption on idempotent reads, shard- local partitioned Bloom filters ( m = 65,536 bits, k = 5 hashes) reject 1,000/1,000 replayed packets IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON CLOUD COMPUTING 2) 3) 4) 3.3 in 0.012 ms at a 0.13% theoretical false-positive rate (v6 ref operational failure abuse audit.csv). Kernel Pooled TCP vs. User-Space Paced UDP Framing: Standard Python aioquic 1.2.0 imple- ments its own classical TLS 1.3 state machine without native ML-KEM/ML-DSA support. Therefore, our fast UDP data path in Track 2 and C1--C3 does not run native PQC-QUIC inside aioquic; instead, after accounting for the hybrid OpenSSL + liboqs session handshake, application payloads traverse a lightweight user-space paced UDP framing layer over SOCK DGRAM (8-byte header !IHH encoding [req id, frag id, n frags], burst pacing, RFC 9002- style adaptive PTO max(24 ms , 1.45 RTT) , and se- lective NACK retransmission of missing fragments). In deployments without kernel QUIC PQC sup- port, symmetric AEAD keys (AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305) are exported from the pooled hybrid TLS 1.3 control channel via RFC 8446 SSL export keying material [25]. SQL/Vector Framing and C-vs.-Python Runtime Confounder: Both SQL point-lookup parameters ( 320 B request, 512 B tuple response) and binary quantized/FP32 vector payloads ( 210 B INT8 vs. 620 B FP32 request for 128 d) are serialized as length-prefixed binary RPC frames forwarded by the server gateway to local PostgreSQL 18.6 sockets. Because user-space UDP packetization and NACK reassembly execute in Python whereas TCP segmen- tation runs in the Linux kernel C stack, the UDP path incurs a measured +3.8 ms local CPU framing penalty on 0% -loss LAN links; this makes UDP wins under 0.5% – 5% WAN packet loss conservative, while motivating native C/Rust QUIC integration (e.g., msquic with oqs-provider) for sub-millisecond LAN deployments. Cross-ISA Native-C Cryptographic Parity: Direct C EVP benchmarks (v6 ref cross isa native c.csv, Fig. S5b) across x86 64 (Intel Ultra 9 185H, AES- NI/AVX2) and Cloud ARM64 (t2a-standard-4, Am- pere Altra Neoverse-N1 Crypto Extensions) con- firm hardware-accelerated AES-256-GCM parity at 1 KiB payloads ( 0.14 – 0.19 µ s, 5.3 – 7.3 Gbps asymp- totic goodput), outperforming ChaCha20-Poly1305 ( 2.1 – 2.6 Gbps) on both ISAs when crypto extensions are present. Explicit Per-Query and Per-Class SLA Formulation To prevent high-accuracy SQL ( 1.00 ) and public HNSW ( ≈ 0.99 ) queries from masking confidential CKKS recall shortfalls under mode-level stream averaging, we define compliance strictly at the individual query level q t with class deadline L max (c t ) = 150 ms for c t ∈ { sql , json , vec } and L max ( conf ) = 250 ms (reporting uniform 150 ms bounds in parallel). Let priv(q t , a t ) ∈ {0, 1} equal 1 iff c t ̸ = conf or action a t evaluates q t homomorphically under CKKS. We 4 separate two explicit per-query indicators: h i S lat-priv (q t ) = I L obs t ≤ L max (c t ) · I [priv(q t , a t ) = 1] · I [c t = conf ∨ A t (q t ) ≥ 0.92] , (1) h i obs S strict-0.92 (q t ) = I L t ≤ L max (c t ) · I [priv(q t , a t ) = 1] · I [A t (q t ) ≥ 0.92] . (2) Equation (1) measures deadline and cryptographic-privacy compliance paired side-by-side with exact confidential Recall@10 conf , whereas Eq. (2) enforces A t (q t ) ≥ 0.92 on every individual query without exception (on discrete Top-10 retrieval where Recall@10(q t ) ∈ {0.0, 0.1, . . . , 1.0} , A t (q t ) ≥ 0.92 requires 10/10 exact neighbors on that query, or Recall@10 conf ≥ 0.92 at the class-cohort level). 4 P UBLIC T IER : A SYMMETRIC INT8 B OUNDS AND M ILLION -S CALE PG18.6 HNSW Compressing a 128 d FP32 query ( 512 B raw + headers > 600 B) into b = 8 -bit asymmetric integers ( 128 B + 8 B scale metadata ≈ 210 B wire frame) ensures single-MTU transmission, and compresses 1024 d RAG embeddings from 4,096 B ( 3 – 4 IP packets) into a single 1,032 B payload within 1,500 B Ethernet MTU [26], [27]. Proposition 1 (Inner-Product Quantization Error: Condi- tional vs. Marginal Variance). Let x ∈ S D−1 ( ∥x∥ 2 = 1 ) be a unit-normalized database vector, and let q ∈ R D be quantized via step size ∆ q = (max i q i − min i q i )/(2 b − 1) , scaled coordinates s i = (q i − q min )/∆ q , and fractional grid offsets u i = s i − ⌊s i ⌋ ∈ [0, 1) , yielding inner-product error E = ⟨ b q − q, x⟩ : 1) 2) Deterministic Nearest-Integer Rounding: On the corpus pair probability space (q, x) ∼ P , under high- resolution locally uniform offsets e i = q b i − q i ∼ U(−∆ q /2, ∆ q /2) with weakly correlated coordi- nates, the marginal variance satisfies Var P (E) ≈ ∆ 2 q P D ∆ 2 q 2 i=1 x i = 12 . 12 Unbiased Stochastic Rounding: For fixed (q, x) , independent draws ξ i ∼ Bernoulli(u i ) satisfy E ξ [E | q, x] = 0 identically and have exact conditional variance Var ξ (E | q, x) = ∆ 2 q D X i=1 x 2 i u i (1 − u i ) ≤ ∆ 2 q , 4 (3) attaining ∆ 2 q /4 iff u i = 1/2 across active coordinates. Taking the expectation over u i ∼ U(0, 1) yields the marginal expected variance E u [Var ξ (E | q, x)] = R P ∆ 2 q 2 1 ∆ 2 q D i=1 x i 0 u(1 − u) du = 6 . Neither result requires isotropy of x since ∥x∥ 22 = 1 . Table 3 and Fig. 2 validate Proposition 1 on 10,000 real SIFT1M [28] and BGE-M3 [2] vector pairs. Crucially, on SIFT1M, 3.26% of pairs exhibit conditional stochastic variance strictly exceeding ∆ 2 q /6 (reaching 0.2036 ∆ 2 q ), while 100.0% obey the sharp bound ∆ 2 q /4 ( 0.25 ∆ 2 q ), confirm- ing the necessity of distinguishing conditional ∆ 2 q /4 from marginal ∆ 2 q /6 . Wire sizes are exact binary KiB ( 1 KiB = 1,024 B; 909.33 KiB = 931,154 B vs. 129.01 KiB = 132,106 B). 1) 2) 3) Index Budget vs. CKKS Noise Loss: Comparing exact FP64 plaintext inner products on the identical candidate lists against decrypted OpenFHE CKKS scores shows |∆R CKKS | ≤ 0.0052 across every row from 5 k to 100 k vectors (maximum inner-product error |∆ IP | ≤ 1.09 × 10 −3 vs. median top-10/11 score gap ∆s 10,11 = 3.8 – 5.9 × 10 −3 ; slight negative ∆R CKKS of −0.002 to −0.005 reflects near-tie bound- ary perturbations within 10 −4 ). Thus, over 99% of confidential recall loss (1 − R CKKS ) originates from coarse cluster candidate truncation ( ∆R index ), not homomorphic approximation noise. Equal-Probe vs. Equal-Candidate-Budget Role of SPANN: Under equal probes ( r = 2 ), SPANN beats unpadded disjoint K-means by +0.1876 ( 95% CI [+0.1735, +0.2017] , d z = +1.165 ) at K c = 96 solely because disjoint clusters average fewer unique candidates ( 113.3 vs. 202.3 ). When disjoint K-means is granted the identical candidate budget ( M = 224 via greedy cluster expansion), disjoint ties SPANN at K c = 96 ( 0.7846 vs. 0.7852 , ∆ = −0.0008 , 95% CI [−0.0158, +0.0142] ) and outperforms SPANN at K c = 192 ( 0.8498 vs. 0.7612 , ∆ = −0.0892 , d z = −0.479 ) because boundary replication consumes slots on duplicate vectors across adjacent centroids ( 155.5 unique out of 224 ). SPANN’s architectural utility is therefore strictly preserving a constant probe count r = 2 over uniform B max buckets without revealing query-dependent variable cluster counts r(q) . Candid Corpus-Scaling Degradation: Holding M = 224 ( r = 2 ) constant keeps server FHE latency constant ( 27.5 – 27.8 ms) from 5 k to 100 k vectors, but Recall@10 drops sharply from 0.7882 ( 5 k) to 0.6364 ( 25 k) and 0.5502 ( 100 k). Doubling the slot budget to M = 512 ( r = 4, B max = 128 , 63.8 ms E2E) achieves the 0.92 target only at N vec = 5,000 ( 0.9216 , 95% CI [0.911, 0.932] ), decaying to 0.8192 ( 25 k) and 0.7322 ( 100 k). RFC 9308 F ALLBACK AND S ILICON E NERGY M ETROLOGY 6.1 Bandit Evaluation Against Stateless RFC 9308 Time- out Fallback At step t , our online controller observes a strictly lagged 5D context vector (frozen hyperparameters in v5 bandit frozen config.json: γ = 0.88, ν = 0.06, λ = 0.08, µ 0 = 0.48, W = 32 ): h x t − = 1, I sql , I conf ,   i ⊤ min RTT t − /300, 2 , min Loss t − /0.10, 2 ∈ R 5 . Crucially, V5 compared bandits against M8 configured as static UDP without TCP fallback, causing M8 to stall at 999.21 ms under UDP policing (C3). Because RFC 9308 [13] explicitly prescribes falling back to TCP upon UDP blocking or throttling, we evaluate a stateless RFC 9308 Timeout- Triggered TCP Fallback Rule (Rule QUIC RFC9308 TCP Fallback: defaults to M8 paced UDP+INT8+1-CT, switches to pooled TCP+1-CT for H ∈ {16, 32, 64} queries after two consecutive > 300 ms UDP stalls or one > 600 ms timeout, and releases hold immediately if TCP stalls). C3 (RFC 9308 Enterprise UDP Policing): When middleboxes rate-police UDP bursts ( 2,186 ms UDP vs. 23 ms TCP), the simple stateless RFC 9308 timeout rule ( H = 32 ) recovers Lat+Priv SLA from 57.81% to 92.41% ( 165.80 ms mean; 92.72% and 150.85 ms at H = 64 ), tying CAPQ D-LinUCB ( 92.69% SLA, 159.29 ms, Wilcoxon p = 0.0840 ). Moreover, Stationary 5D LinUCB ( γ = 1.00 ) out- performs D-LinUCB ( 30.09 vs. 37.21 regret, 94.47% SLA, 141.60 ms, p95 = 279.5 ms): because the 5D context includes lagged probe RTT ( 2,024.7 ms under policing), linear context separation plus the feasibility gate—not exponential forgetting γ = 0.88 —drives adaptation, while discounting forgets pre-policing wireless history and re-explores suboptimal arms. 6.2 Silicon RAPL Energy Metrology and Idle-Drift Uncer- tainty Limits Table 6 and Fig. 5(b) report continuous C++ OpenFHE pack- age energy via Intel hardware RAPL (rapl package0 pkg) with JCGM GUM [29], [30] expanded uncertainty U 95 . Client edge energy in Track 1 reflects client-side RAPL CPU active energy excluding passive WAN radio wait, explaining why US-Central active CPU en- ergy ( 46.4 mJ for M5, matching v2 wan 3regions summary mbb ci.csv) is lower than low-RTT high- duty-cycle regional bursts. Unified Cloud CPU + Egress Cost Model: Earlier versions billed only server vCPU time + compact payload estimates in Track 1 ( ∼ $0.25 – $1.11/10 6 queries) while billing full serialized RNS cipher- text egress in Track 2. Applying the identical regional GCP pricing formula C t = r vcpu T t, srv + r egress W t, resp ($ 0.2264 /$ 0.2216 /$ 0.1896 per vCPU- h and $ 0.12 /$ 0.12 /$ 0.085 per GiB egress in Bangkok/Singapore/US-Central) reconciles both tracks: Multi-CT modes cost $18.65 – $32.01/10 6 queries, whereas 1-CT slot aggregation cuts cloud egress cost to $10.86 – $15.29/10 6 queries in Track 2 (and $3.53 – $4.79 in Track 1 where con- fidential queries constitute 25% alongside compact public responses). Per-Class Confidential SLA Reality in Track 2 ( M = 224 ): In Track 2 (calibrated netns + tc netem shaped at 300 Mbps / 0.15% loss in Bangkok, 250 Mbps / 0.25% loss in Singapore, and 200 Mbps / 0.30% loss in US-Central; 25% sql, 50% vec 128d, 25% conf at N = 5 k , K c = 96, M = 224 ), confiden- tial Recall@10 is 0.7852 – 0.7856 for SPANN modes (M1, M7, M8, M5), 0.5968 for M6 ( r = 2 disjoint), and 0.4120 for M4 ( r = 1 disjoint). Under strict per- query A t (q t ) ≥ 0.92 (Eq. 2), every M = 224 mode scores 0.0% on the confidential class, capping overall stream strict SLA at the 75.0% non-confidential ceil- ing. Evaluating pure confidential latency compliance ( ≤ 250 ms) side-by-side with actual recall shows that in Bangkok all pooled CKKS modes (M4, M6, M7, M8, M5) achieve 100.0% ≤ 250 ms delivery, while in Singapore single-CT UDP modes (M8, M5) raise confidential ≤ 250 ms delivery from 8.3% (M7 Multi-CT TCP) to 79.2% ( 92.04 and 94.67 ms mean vs. 359.61 ms). Track 2 omits synthetic mode-constant energy numbers; hardware-measured RAPL package energy is reported directly in Table 6. 311.28 ms in US-Central ( +67.2% , p95 = 2,091.44 vs. 616.82 ms). Query-level tail inspection con- firms that median latency in US-Central is virtually identical ( 230.07 ms for M5 vs. 229.68 ms for M8), because 225.5 ms physical 1-RTT plus 31 ms FHE compute inherently exceeds 250 ms ( 0% confidential SLA for all modes). However, UCB exploration ( ν = 0.06 ) occasionally samples pooled TCP arms across the 225.5 ms transcontinental path, triggering 15/96 multi-second TCP HOL retransmission stalls ( > 700 ms) in M5 compared to only 4/96 loss tail events in static UDP M8. Thus, on stationary links without UDP middlebox policing, static M8 (paired with a passive RFC 9308 timeout fallback) strictly dominates online bandit exploration. 8 L IMITATIONS Five scope boundaries govern our findings: (i) at fixed candidate budget M = 224 , confidential CKKS Recall@10 falls from 0.788 ( 5 k) to 0.550 ( 100 k), and reaching 0.922 even at 5 k requires doubling budget to M = 512 ( 63.8 ms); (ii) our fast UDP data path uses Python user-space paced framing rather than native C/Rust kernel PQC-QUIC, in- troducing a +3.8 ms local runtime confounder relative to C OpenSSL/TCP; (iii) padded cluster routing still leaks Zipfian query-frequency distributions (A3: 100% top-5 cluster match) unless mitigated by ORAM or dummy traffic; (iv) 1-CT slot aggregation improves latency only below the 423 – 464 Mbps downlink crossover; and (v) hardware RAPL measures CPU package energy (excluding NIC/cellular radio transceivers) and suffers wide U 95 intervals during long low-thread runs due to OS background idle drift. 9 C ONCLUSION This empirical study decoupled transport, quantization, homomorphic aggregation, and online control effects across PQC-hardened vector-relational streams. Persistent hybrid PQC session pooling ( +52.15 pp SLA) and single-MTU INT8 quantization ( 5.39 × – 22.76× tighter 95% error bounds) deliver the primary latency gains. In the confidential tier, N = 8192 1-CT slot aggregation cuts response traffic 7.05× (beneficial below 426 Mbps downlink), while plaintext-vs.- CKKS controls prove that corpus-scaling recall degradation stems from candidate-slot budgets rather than CKKS noise. Finally, static pooled UDP+INT8+1-CT paired with a state- less RFC 9308 timeout-to-TCP fallback suffices on normal and policed paths, positioning contextual bandits as specialized controllers for complex multi-regime policies rather than universal replacements for protocol engineering.
